results.title: News – Line at Queens food pantry stretches for 8 blocks - Elmcor
results.content:
Skip to content



CORONA, Queens (WABC) — Nearly two months into the pandemic, the strain on some families is at an all-time high. With no jobs and no income, some have no way to pay rent and even putting food on the table is difficult.

Demand for food assistance is rising at an extraordinary rate, and at a food pantry in Queens on Wednesday, the line stretched for eight blocks.

At one of the hardest-hit communities in Corona, a food pantry at Elmcor, located on Northern Boulevard, opens at noon on Wednesdays and goes until 4 p.m., or until they run out of food. Last week, they served at least 540 families.

results.title: Food Pantry | New Life CDC
results.content:
Our Food Pantry serves the Elmhurst and Corona community’s homeless and low-income residents with hot meals-to-go and weekly deliveries of non-perishable food and fresh produce to those that continue to be food insecure. Nearly two in three children in Elmhurst and Corona live in households in or near poverty and wage earners typically work disproportionately in lower-wage professions mainly in construction and hospitality-related sectors. 62% of Elmhurst and Corona residents are rent burdened, a higher rate than residents citywide. Rent burdened households pay more than 30% of their income for housing and may have difficulty affording food, clothing, transportation and health care. Since the pandemic, many are still unemployed or are working reduced hours. [...] Tuesdays, 5 pm - 7 pm  /  Saturdays, 10 am - 12 pm

 Weekly Grocery Deliveries for low-income families
